title: [finding] `check:cross-package-test-inputs` cannot red an undeclared tree-scoped walk inside an already-declared package — the seed escape depth is computed but never asserted
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` PM seat, session `session_019RfFHiRCSs3JXLK4cwcfox` (`os-steve`), while landing the playbook half of #15528. Filed unassigned, for triage.

#15528 asked whether the retirement playbook's tree-scoped absence-pin mandate could be made hashable. The playbook half landed: the mandate now also requires the pin's walk radius to be declared in `CROSS_PACKAGE_TEST_INPUTS`. **That rule is prose, and prose is the only thing holding it** — this card is the mechanical half that would make an undeclared radius fail instead.

## What stays green that should not

`scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` `verify()` asks five questions, all measured on `8e18931dd`:

1. an escaping package with no table entry — RED
2. a table entry whose package no longer has an escaping test — RED (stale)
3. a repo-relative literal the tests NAME that no declared glob covers — RED
4. a declared glob nothing holds (`globHolderVerdict`, no roster hit and no live `heldBy` witness) — RED
5. `turbo.json` missing a `PKG#test` input for a declared glob — RED

None of the five asks the question a tree-scoped pin raises: **does this package contain a walk whose radius exceeds its declared globs?** A `readdirSync` descent on a loop variable NAMES no literal, so limb 3 sees nothing; it ADDS no glob, so limbs 4 and 5 see nothing; and in a package that already carries an entry (`@objectstack/spec` does), limbs 1 and 2 are already satisfied by the package's other escaping tests.

⇒ A new tree-scoped absence pin can land in `packages/spec` with its whole radius unhashed, and this gate exits 0 naming nothing. That is the Layer A / Layer B blind spot the gate's own header opens with, re-entered one grain below where the gate looks.

## The input the assertion needs already exists

The gate computes the seed's escape DEPTH for the escape verdict (`walkLiteral` / the `pathExpression` resolver) and deliberately keeps the depth when it cannot recover the name — its header states it: *"an unreadable argument costs the name and keeps the depth, so the escape verdict is unaffected"*. So the missing limb has its input already:

> for each escaping test, when a directory-walking descent is rooted at a seed whose depth climbs above the package root, require that seed's subtree to be covered by a declared glob — judged on the SEED, not on the names the walk produces.

That is a judging-logic change, which is why it was held out of #15528's PR rather than folded in.

## What it would cost, stated honestly, because it is the reason this is a card and not a patch

An honest whole-repo radius for the mandated pin is every `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` / `.mjs` / `.cjs` / `.mts` / `.cts` / `.json` / `.md` / `.mdx` / `.yaml` / `.yml` outside `node_modules` / `dist` / `.git` / `.turbo` / `.cache` / `.objectstack` / `coverage`. Two problems, both measured:

- **The table's grammar cannot express the exclusions.** Entries are positive globs only; `expectedInputs()` prefixes each with `$TURBO_ROOT$/` verbatim, and the negations it emits (`!dist/**`, `!coverage/**`, `!.turbo/**`) are package-local and fixed. A `!`-prefixed entry would be required in `turbo.json` as the literal `$TURBO_ROOT$/!...`.
- **The positive-roots spelling is expensive.** Adding `examples/**` alone to `@objectstack/spec#test` moved its hashed input set from 2875 to 3150 files (turbo dry-run, measured). The declaration file's own commentary repeatedly refuses radii that put a suite on every docs PR, and an honest whole-repo radius is exactly that.

So the limb above should probably arrive together with a decision about what the mandated walk is ALLOWED to reach — narrowing the mandate and asserting the narrower radius may be cheaper than declaring the wide one. That is triage's call, not this card's.

Refs: #15528 (the playbook half, and the review condition it came from) · #15233 and #15234 (sibling findings on the same gate family, unrelated defects)
